$comment: Controlled vocabulary for CISA-CD-004. The CISA 2026 elements say the Component Hash Algorithm should be identified using IANA Hash Function Textual Names. Neither CycloneDX nor SPDX uses those names in its own enumeration, so a validator that checks the IANA registry literally will reject almost every real file. The mapping below is how CISA-CD-004 is actually implemented: accept the format's own enum, normalise to the IANA name where one exists, and flag only algorithms that map to nothing.
registrationPolicy: Standards Action. Registration requires a standards-track RFC which updates or obsoletes RFC 3279.

ianaRegistry.name: md5
ianaRegistry.note: Broken for collision resistance. Flag any use.

ianaRegistry.name: sha-1
ianaRegistry.note: Withdrawn by NIST for most uses. Flag.

cyclonedx.$comment: CycloneDX hash-alg enum. Values with an IANA equivalent normalise to it; null means the algorithm is real and usable but has no IANA registration, which is not the author's fault and must not be reported as an error.

implementerNote: Three outcomes, and conflating them is the mistake. (1) The value maps to an IANA name: pass. (2) The value is in the format's enum but maps to null: pass with an informational note that no IANA registration exists, because the author did nothing wrong. (3) The value is in neither: that is the finding. Separately, md2, md5 and sha-1 pass the vocabulary check and should still raise a weak-algorithm warning, which is a different rule from CISA-CD-004 and is not in this pack.
